reason: Every persistent truth surface and durable key namespace in production code, registered once at the guard landing. A new persistent write or *Prefix constant must add a reviewed entry before it can pass; the checker has no auto-write mode.

surfaces.reason: The configuration chain is the single truth for declaration and publication facts.

Settlement facts are the live truth; the legacy delivery record is the read-only migration input, and the retry-attempt facts share the settlement family so a restart continues the redrive count instead of resetting it.
Host-owned approvals and runtime directories under the configured workspace.
Per-run trajectory capture root and its bounded swap directory.
Denial and goal event identities are ordered on the durable ledger; the budget window is its persisted snapshot.
The reflection anchor record carries the state machine's durable position.
Training-capture record files, seal marker and swapped request snapshots.

The local-file KV tier keeps one durable unit: an append-only journal of checksummed frames, which journal.go opens and appends to, and which the tier's key-value view reads as its key order. A torn tail is cut at open and a mismatched frame refuses the open, so no snapshot or shard becomes a second truth.

Event segment, index and metadata keys are one durable KV layout. The tier's fact surface and its external-KV adapter reach the store only through the AtomicStore port, so they write no key layout of their own and are covered by review, not by this static scan.
Age-fold product facts are addressed by these durable key prefixes.
The five durable record kinds share one KV face; the carrier tables they rebuild are the one truth of the tasks a process serves.
Migrated legacy records carry this durable archive identity namespace.
Attention, handoff and reactivation identities are durable fact-chain identities, not a second store.
Approval request files and the evidence mirror are durable across restarts.
Retirement of a superseded generation is a chain record keyed gen-retire:<id>; release itself stays with the retirement ledger drain (ADR 0007 / Q2).

A framework checkpoint is filed under checkpoint:<partitionSeq> and read back by the frozen event type: the key is the partition sequence the cut advanced to and the payload carries the state slices, so the fact itself is the only truth of the state it states.

content_addressed_artifacts.reason: ArchiveDigest is the tree digest of the source the import read, and each migrated original records that digest beside its key and length; the archived material is never its own truth.

content_address_exempt.reason: ageKey hashes the fold inputs to mint the product's identity: the digest is the key itself, and no stored material is read back against it.
FactKey hashes the fact type and identity to mint a key; nothing is verified against the digest.

CheckpointFor hashes the payload to mint the checkpoint's own identity: the digest is the identity the payload states, the reader recomputes it over the payload it read, and no stored material is referenced or verified against it.
